entrypoints.summary: The stock-check HTTP request carries a URL in the stockApi form parameter.
The lab solution directs the user to change stockApi to an internal 192.168.0.X address and port 8080.

observability.positive_marker: A single scan entry with status 200 shows an admin interface.

preconditions: A reachable lab stock-check feature accepts stockApi.
The lab's internal 192.168.0.X range contains an administrative interface on port 8080.

trigger_steps.summary: Replace stockApi with an internal admin URL and vary the final IPv4 octet from 1 through 255 to scan for the interface.
For the discovered host, change the stockApi path to the documented account-deletion endpoint.

capabilities.concept: server-side request to internal back-end URL

relation_candidates.dst: server-side request to internal back-end URL
relation_candidates.rationale: The lab directs changing stockApi to an internal address, and the SSRF topic explains that this parameter causes a server request to the specified URL.

The documented scan finds an admin interface on an internal address, and topic material explains that server interaction with non-user-reachable back ends can expose sensitive unauthenticated functionality.
relation_candidates.src: server-side request to internal back-end URL

relation_candidates.rationale: After locating the interface, the lab directs changing stockApi to the admin deletion path for carlos.
This relation expresses the primary invariant inferred from the demonstrated arbitrary internal destination selection; no implementation or patch is supplied.
relation_candidates.src: server-side request to internal back-end URL

impact.affected_asset: Internal administrative interface and the user account named carlos in the lab instance.
impact.attacker_capability: Cause the application to scan an internal address range and send a request to the discovered admin delete path.
impact.security_effect: Unauthorized access to an internal administrative interface and deletion of an account in the documented lab.

causal_trace.summary: A remote user can modify the stockApi parameter submitted by the stock-check functionality to contain a chosen URL.
The stock-check URL-fetching capability accepts an internal back-end destination, rather than constraining user-supplied destinations to the intended stock service.
The server-side stock check fetches the selected internal URL; the lab directs scanning 192.168.0.X on port 8080 for an admin interface and then requesting its delete endpoint.
The requester obtains access to an internal administrative interface and can invoke deletion of the user carlos in the lab scenario.

failure.operation: Server-side HTTP fetch of an attacker-selected internal administrative URL through stockApi.

primary_invariant.statement: A user-controlled stockApi value must not cause the application to fetch arbitrary internal back-end administrative destinations.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The documented solution replaces stockApi with internal 192.168.0.X:8080/admin URLs and identifies an administrative interface through the resulting server-side requests.

quality.review_notes: This is a PortSwigger instructional lab and conceptual SSRF material, not project source, a patch, or an observed execution transcript. The described HTTP status is a lab oracle/expected result, not evidence that this extraction executed the lab. No negative control, target implementation identity, immutable version, or remediation artifact is supplied.

remediation.invariant_restored: The supplied materials do not document a patch or deployed mitigation; the required invariant is that stockApi cannot select internal administrative destinations.
